akhfash:16-16.t: He said ﴿وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافاً﴾: its singular is "اللِّفُّ".

akhfash:26-26.t: And He said ﴿جَزَآءً وِفَاقاً﴾: He means "it matched their deeds in exact accord" (وافَقَ أهْمالَهُم وِفاقا), as you say "قاتَل قِتالا". «[Translator's note: the source writes «أهمالهم»; presumably «أعمالهم», "their deeds".]»

akhfash:28-28.t: And He said ﴿وَكَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّاباً﴾: because its verb has four (letters), He wanted to make it like the pattern "أَفعَلْتُ" — "إِفْعالاً", so He said ﴿كِذَّاباً﴾, making it match the number (of letters) of its maṣdar (verbal noun). On this analogy you say "قاتل" — "قِيتَالا", and it is part of the speech of the Arabs.

akhfash:29-29.t: And He said ﴿وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ كِتَاباً﴾: He made ﴿كلَّ﴾ accusative even though the verb is occupied with the hāʾ (the pronoun), because what precedes it has had a verb operate on it, so He made it run in the same way and had an implied verb govern it.

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ ٱلْمَرْءُ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ﴾: if you wish, you make it "he looks (to see) what thing his hands have sent forth" (ينظر أيّ شيء قدّمت يداه), and its description (ṣifa) is "قدمت". And some said: "It is only 'he looks to what his hands have sent forth' (ينظر الى ما قدمت يداه)", and "إلى" ("to") was dropped.

daas-irab:1-5.t: ﴿عَمَّ﴾: composed of ﴿عن﴾, a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾, interrogative, in the position of a genitive by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿عَنِ النَّبَإِ﴾: attached to an omitted verb; ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a second adjective; ﴿هُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿فِيهِ﴾: attached to the khabar (predicate) ﴿مُخْتَلِفُونَ﴾; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي. ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿سَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾: the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw being its agent; the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of an omitted verb of saying. The verse after it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:6-11.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مِهاداً﴾: second direct object; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَالْجِبالَ أَوْتاداً﴾: both conjoined to الأرض مهادا. ﴿وَخَلَقْناكُمْ﴾: a past verb, its agent and its object; ﴿أَزْواجاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿نَوْمَكُمْ﴾: first direct object; ﴿سُباتاً﴾: second direct object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِباساً﴾ and ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهارَ مَعاشاً﴾: both conjoined to what precedes them.

daas-irab:12-16.t: ﴿وَبَنَيْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿فَوْقَكُمْ﴾: an adverb of place; ﴿سَبْعاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿شِداداً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, and the one following it is conjoined to it. ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنا﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿مِنَ الْمُعْصِراتِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿ماءً﴾: direct object; ﴿ثَجَّاجاً﴾: adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِنُخْرِجَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of reason (taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزلنا; ﴿بِهِ﴾: attached to نخرج; ﴿حَبًّا﴾: direct object; ﴿وَنَباتاً﴾: conjoined to حبا; ﴿وَجَنَّاتٍ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿أَلْفافاً﴾: adjective.

daas-irab:17-20.t: ﴿إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ﴾: inna and its noun, which is muḍāf to الفصل; ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿مِيقاتاً﴾: its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن… is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: badal (substitute) for يوم الفصل; ﴿يُنْفَخُ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent; ﴿فِي الصُّورِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فَتَأْتُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿أَفْواجاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَفُتِحَتِ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿السَّماءُ﴾: deputy agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَكانَتْ﴾: kāna, its noun being latent; ﴿أَبْواباً﴾: its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. The verse following it is conjoined to it and its i'rab is like it.

daas-irab:21-26.t: ﴿إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿كانَتْ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿مِرْصاداً﴾: the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِلطَّاغِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) مرصادا; ﴿مَآباً﴾: a second khabar of كانت. ﴿لابِثِينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to what precedes them; ﴿أَحْقاباً﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَذُوقُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿بَرْداً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَلا شَراباً﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿حَمِيماً﴾: badal (substitute) for شرابا; ﴿غَسَّاقاً﴾: conjoined to حميما. ﴿جَزاءً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿وِفاقاً﴾: naʿt (adjective).

daas-irab:27-30.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَرْجُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿حِساباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا, the clause كانوا is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl). ﴿وَكَذَّبُوا﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿كِذَّاباً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿كُلَّ﴾: accusative by ishtighāl (a noun governed by an omitted verb that the following verb explains); ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿أَحْصَيْناهُ﴾: a past verb, its agent and its object; ﴿كِتاباً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause explains the omitted one, and the omitted clause is parenthetical. ﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَلَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is a particle of reason; ﴿نَزِيدَكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, its agent latent (mustatir), and the kāf is the first direct object; ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿عَذاباً﴾: second direct object; the verbal clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:31-36.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾: the fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿مَفازاً﴾: its postponed noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿حَدائِقَ﴾: badal (substitute) for مفازا; ﴿أَعْناباً﴾: conjoined to حدائق; ﴿وَكَواعِبَ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿أَتْراباً﴾: naʿt (adjective) of كواعب; ﴿وَكَأْساً دِهاقاً﴾: both conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿لَغْواً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿لا﴾ is negative; ﴿كِذَّاباً﴾: conjoined to لغوا; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿جَزاءً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: attached to جزاء; ﴿عَطاءً﴾: badal for جزاء; ﴿حِساباً﴾: adjective of عطاء.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿رَبِّ السَّماواتِ﴾: badal (substitute) for ربك, muḍāf to السموات; ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: conjoined to السموات; ﴿وَما﴾: conjoined to السموات; ﴿بَيْنَهُمَا﴾: an adverb of place; ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾: badal for رب. ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَمْلِكُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿مِنْهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿خِطاباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ﴾: an adverb of time, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿وَالْمَلائِكَةُ﴾: conjoined to الروح; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿صَفًّا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَتَكَلَّمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مَنْ﴾: badal (substitute) for the wāw in يتكلمون; ﴿أَذِنَ﴾: a past verb; ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الرَّحْمنُ﴾: agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿وَقالَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); ﴿صَواباً﴾: naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الْيَوْمُ﴾: its khabar (predicate); ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of اليوم; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and ﴿من﴾ is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿اتَّخَذَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿إِلى رَبِّهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) ﴿مَآباً﴾; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position, and the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من.

daas-irab:40-40.t:
[Translator's note: the Arabic source text of this entry is garbled (the opening letters of most quoted words and their brackets are lost, e.g. «ِنَّا»», «وَذاباً»», «وا»»); the quoted words are restored below from the verse (إِنَّا أَنْذَرْناكُمْ عَذاباً قَرِيباً يَوْمَ يَنْظُرُ الْمَرْءُ ما قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ وَيَقُولُ الْكافِرُ يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُراباً) and the analysis is translated as written.]
﴿إِنَّا﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿أَنْذَرْناكُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first object; ﴿عَذاباً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿قَرِيباً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿يَنْظُرُ﴾: an imperfect verb; ﴿الْمَرْءُ﴾: its agent; ﴿ما﴾: direct object; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ﴾: a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿وَيَقُولُ الْكافِرُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يا﴾: a particle drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿لَيْتَنِي﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); the nūn is for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is its noun; ﴿كُنْتُ﴾: kāna and its noun; ﴿تُراباً﴾: its khabar; the verbal clause is the khabar of layta, and the nominal clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

farraa:1-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَمَّ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ﴾.
It is said: About what thing are they asking one another? — meaning Quraysh. Then He said to His Prophet ﷺ: they are asking one another about the great news, meaning the Qur'an. It is also said: about what Quraysh are talking regarding the Qur'an. Then He answered, so that عم يتساءلون became as though [in the meaning of]: for what reason are they asking one another about the Qur'an? Then He informed and said: ﴿ٱلَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ — between one who affirms it and one who denies it; that is their disagreement. The readers agreed on the yāʾ in His saying: ﴿كَلاَّ سَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾. Al-Ḥasan alone read: "كلا ستعلمون", and that is correct. It is like His saying — even though there is no "say" before it [here] —: ﴿قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَتُغْلَبُونَ﴾ and سَيُغْلَبُون.
His saying: ﴿ثَجَّاجاً﴾: like the mouths of water-skins (العزالي): [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here.]

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَفُتِحَتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَاباً﴾.
Like: ﴿إِذَا السَّماءُ انْشَقَّتْ﴾ and ﴿وإذا السماءُ فُرِجَتْ﴾; the meaning is one, and Allah knows best. That is how the exegesis has come.

farraa:23-23.t:
[123/a] His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّبِثِينَ فِيهَآ أَحْقَاباً﴾.
I was told from al-Aʿmash that he said: It reached us from ʿAlqama that he read "لَبِثين", and that is the reading of the companions of ʿAbdullāh. People since then read (لابثين), and it is the better of the two, because (لابثين), when it is in a position where it acts and puts [something] in the accusative, has the alif, like: الطامع (the one who covets) and الباخل (the one who withholds) shortly. اللَّبِث is the slow one, and it is permissible, as one says: رجل طمِعٌ and طامع (a covetous man). If you said: هذا طمِعٌ فيما قِبَلك (this one covets what you have), it would be permissible. Labīd said:
أوْ مِسْحَلٌ عَملٌ عضادةَ سَمْحَجٍ * بسَرَاتِها نَدَبٌ له وكُلومُ
(Or a braying wild ass, busy at the flank of a long-backed she-ass, on whose back are scars and wounds from him.)
So he made عمل act upon العضادة; had it been عامل, it would have been clearer in Arabic. Likewise when you say of a man: ضرّابٌ and ضروبٌ (a great striker), you do not make them act upon anything, because they are [words of] praise; but when the poet needs to make them act, he does so. Someone recited to me:
* وبالفأسِ ضرَّابٌ رءوس الكرانفِ *
(And with the axe, a great striker of the bases of palm-stalks.)
Its singular is كرنافة, which are the bases of the roof [Translator's note: so in the source; الكرانيف are usually the broad bases of palm fronds]. It is said: الحُقْب is eighty years, the year being three hundred and sixty days, each day of which is a thousand years by the reckoning of the people of this world.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْداً وَلاَ شَرَاباً﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying]: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: they taste in it neither the coolness of drink nor drink. Some said: they do not taste in it any coolness (برداً), meaning sleep. Al-Farrāʾ said: sleep does cool the one who has it; the thirsty one sleeps and is cooled by sleep.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿جَزَآءً وِفَاقاً﴾.
In accordance with their deeds.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّاباً﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, read it lightened: "كِذَاباً", while ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, the people of Medina and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī made it heavy (doubled).
It is an eloquent Yemeni dialect: they say كذبت به كِذَّاباً (I denied it utterly), and خرّقت القميص خِرّاقاً (I tore the shirt to pieces); every فعّلت has, in their dialect, a maṣdar on the pattern فِعّال, doubled. One of their Bedouins said to me [123/b] at al-Marwa, asking me for a legal ruling: "Is shaving (الحلق) dearer to you, or shortening (القِصّار)?"
One of Banū Kilāb recited to me:
لقدْ طالَ ما ثَبَّطْتَنِى عنْ صَحابتىِ * وعن حِوَجٍ قِضَّاؤها من شِفائيا
(Long indeed have you held me back from my companions and from needs whose fulfilment is my cure.)
Al-Kisāʾī used to read lightened: ﴿لا يَسْمَعون فِيهَا لغْوا ولا كِذَاباً﴾ (35), because it is not tied to a verb that makes it a maṣdar; and he read doubled: ﴿وَكَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّاباً﴾, because كذّبوا ties الكذّاب to being a maṣdar. What he said is good. Its meaning: they hear no idle talk in it — He means: falsehood — nor كذاب, i.e. they do not call one another liars.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَّبِّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It is put in the genitive in its case-ending, and also in the nominative. Likewise: ﴿ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ لاَ يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَاباً﴾: "الرحمنُ" is put in the nominative and [also] in the genitive in its case-ending; the nominative in it is more common. He said: al-Farrāʾ reads (ربِّ) in the genitive and "الرحمنُ" in the nominative.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Nabaʾ
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾: its origin is «عَنْ ما يَتَساءَلُونَ؟!»; the nūn was assimilated into the mīm because the mīm shares with the nūn the nasal resonance (ghunna). We have explained earlier in the book why the alif was dropped. The meaning is: "About what thing are they asking one another?!" The wording is that of a question, but the meaning is to magnify the matter, as you say «أيُّ شَيْءٍ زَيْدٌ» ("what a thing Zayd is!"). Then He made it clear, saying: ﴿عَنِ النَّبَإ العَظِيمِ﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 2]. It was said that it is the Qur'an; it was said: about the resurrection; and it was said: about the matter of the Prophet ﷺ. What indicates it is His saying ﴿إنَّ يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ كانَ مِيقاتًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 17], which indicates that they were asking one another about the resurrection.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿كَلا سَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — it was also read «كَلّا سَتَعْلَمُونَ» with tāʾ. What the readers follow is «كَلّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ» with yāʾ, and it is better; the tāʾ is transmitted from al-Ḥasan.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿ألَمْ نَجْعَلِ الأرْضَ مِهادًا﴾ — it was also read «مَهْدًا», but most readers read it ﴿مِهادًا﴾, and the meaning is the same. Its interpretation is: We made it submissive for them so that they dwell on it and travel through its tracts.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿وَخَلَقْناكم أزْواجًا﴾: He created the male and the female. It was also said: «أزْواجًا», that is: kinds.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا نَوْمَكم سُباتًا﴾: «اَلسُّباتُ» is that one is cut off from movement while the spirit is in his body; that is: We made your sleep a rest for you.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا اللَّيْلَ لِباسًا﴾, that is: you find repose in it, and it wraps around you.

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿وَبَنَيْنا فَوْقَكم سَبْعًا شِدادًا﴾, that is: seven heavens.

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا سِراجًا وهّاجًا﴾, that is: We placed the sun in them as a lamp. The interpretation of ﴿وَهّاجًا﴾ is: blazing.

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَأنْـزَلْنا مِنَ المُعْصِراتِ ماءً ثَجّاجًا﴾: «اَلْمُعْصِراتُ» are the clouds, because they press out (taʿṣir) the water. It was also said: «اَلْمُعْصِراتُ» is as one says «قَدْ أُجِزَّ الزَّرْعُ، فَهو مُجَزٌّ» ("the crop is ripe for cutting") — when it reaches the point of being rained from, it has «أعْصَرَ». The meaning of «ثَجّاجٌ» is: pouring.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا ونَباتًا﴾: everything that is harvested is grain (ḥabb), and every pasture that livestock eat is vegetation (nabāt).

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿وَجَنّاتٍ ألْفافًا﴾, that is: and gardens with intertwined trees. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known what He created and that He is able to resurrect, and said: ﴿إنَّ يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ كانَ مِيقاتًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 17].

zajjaj:18-18.t:
﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ﴾ is a badal (substitute) from «يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ»; if you wish, it is an explanation of «يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ». We have explained «اَلصُّورُ» earlier. ﴿فَتَأْتُونَ أفْواجًا﴾, that is: every community comes with its leader.
﴿وَفُتِحَتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ أبْوابًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 19], that is: it is split open, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 1], ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْشَقَّتْ﴾ [al-Inshiqāq: 1].

zajjaj:21-22.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كانَتْ مِرْصادًا﴾ ﴿لِلطّاغِينَ مَآبًا﴾, that is: it lies in wait for the people of unbelief and for whoever has deserved the punishment; it almost bursts with rage, and none upon whom the word of punishment has been realised passes beyond it. The meaning of ﴿مَآبًا﴾ is: to it they are returned.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿لابِثِينَ فِيها أحْقابًا﴾, and «لَبِثِينَ» (also read): one says «لَبِثَ الرَّجُلُ، فَهو لابِثٌ» ("the man stayed, so he is staying"), and one says «هُوَ لُبْثٌ بِمَكانِ كَذا», that is: staying has become his habit. «اَلْأحْقابُ», its singular is «حُقْبٌ», and «اَلْحُقْبُ» is eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, and each day equal in length to a thousand years of the years of this world. The meaning is that they remain for ages, not tasting during those ages any coolness or drink, while they abide in the Fire forever, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: «خالِدِينَ فِيها أبَدًا».

zajjaj:24-24.t: The meaning of ﴿لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها بَرْدًا﴾: it was said: sleep. And it may be: "they taste therein no coolness of wind, nor of shade, nor of sleep."

zajjaj:25-25.t:
﴿إلا حَمِيمًا وغَسّاقًا﴾, that is: they taste nothing therein except boiling water (ḥamīm), which is at the extreme of heat.
As for «اَلْغَسّاقُ», it was said: what oozes (yaghsiq) from their skins, that is, flows. And it was said: «اَلْغَسّاقُ» is what is intensely cold.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿جَزاءً وِفاقًا﴾, that is: they were requited in accordance with their deeds.

zajjaj:27-27.t: ﴿إنَّهم كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ حِسابًا﴾, that is: they do not believe in the resurrection, nor that they will be brought to account and hope for the reward of a reckoning.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا كِذّابًا﴾: this is the majority reading. It was also read «كِذابًا» without doubling. ﴿كِذّابًا﴾ with doubling is more frequent, and among the maṣdars (verbal nouns) of the pattern «فَعَّلْتُ» it is better than «فِعالٌ». The poet said:
؎لَقَدْ طالَ ما رَيَّثَتْنِي عَنْ صَحابَتِي ∗∗∗ وعَنْ حِوَجٍ قَضّاؤُها مِن شِفائِيا
(Long indeed has she held me back from my companions, and from needs whose fulfilment would be my cure.)
— from «قَضَيْتُ قَضاءً». And like «كِذابًا» without doubling is the saying of the poet:
؎فَصَدَقْتُها وكَذَّبْتُها ∗∗∗ والمَرْءُ يَنْفَعُهُ كِذابُهْ
(I told her the truth and I lied to her, and a man may profit from his lying.)

zajjaj:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أحْصَيْناهُ كِتابًا﴾: «وَكُلَّ» is accusative through an implied (muḍmar) verb which «أحْصَيْناهُ كِتابًا» explains; the meaning is: "and We have enumerated everything — We have enumerated it."
His saying ﴿كِتابًا﴾ is tawkīd (emphasis) of His saying «أحْصَيْناهُ», because the meaning of «أحْصَيْناهُ» and «كَتَبْناهُ», as regards what is obtained and established, is one; so the meaning is: "We wrote it down in writing."

zajjaj:34-34.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَكَأْسًا دِهاقًا﴾, that is: the implied structure of the verse is "they did not hope for the reward of a reckoning", so there is an omitted muḍāf there.
«[Translator's note: this sentence on the omitted muḍāf concerns verse 27 (﴿لا يَرْجُونَ حِسابًا﴾), not verse 34; it is translated where the source places it.]»
Abū Isḥāq said: "Al-kaʾs: every vessel containing drink is a kaʾs, and if there is no drink in it, it is not a kaʾs. Likewise al-māʾida: whatever table has food upon it is a māʾida." The meaning of «دِهاقًا» is: full. It has also come in the exegesis that it is pure. The poet said:
؎يَلَذُّهُ بِكَأْسِهِ الدِّهاقُ
(He relishes it in his brimming cup.)

zajjaj:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿جَزاءً مِن رَبِّكَ عَطاءً حِسابًا﴾: it is accusative through the meaning of «إنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفازًا»; the meaning is: "He requited them with that as a requital." Likewise ﴿عَطاءً حِسابًا﴾, because the meaning of «أعْطاهُمْ» and «جَزاهُمْ» is one. «حِسابًا» means: what suffices them, that is: in it is what they desire. One says «أحْسَبَنِي كَذا وكَذا» in the sense of: it sufficed me.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿رَبِّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: it was read in the genitive as an attribute, following His saying «مِن رَبِّكَ رَبِّ», and it was read «رَبُّ» in the sense "He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth". Likewise «اَلرَّحْمَنُ» ﴿لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنهُ خِطابًا﴾ was read in the genitive and the nominative, and its explanation is the explanation of «رَبِّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ».

zajjaj:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ والمَلائِكَةُ صَفًّا﴾: «اَلرُّوحُ» is a creation like humans, but it is not human. It was also said: «اَلرُّوحُ» is Jibrīl, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿فَمَن شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إلى رَبِّهِ مَآبًا﴾, that is: a place of return.

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الكافِرُ يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُرابًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that on the Day of Resurrection retaliation will be taken for the hornless animal (al-jammāʾ) from the horned one — «اَلْجَمّاءُ» is the one that has no horn — then Allah the Exalted will make them all dust, and that dust is the darkness (al-qatara) that covers the faces of the unbelievers and rises over their faces; so the unbeliever wishes that he were dust. It has also been said that the meaning of ﴿يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُرابًا﴾ is: would that I had not been resurrected, as He said: ﴿يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 25].
